title: Illustrative example: five alternatives, four criteria

source.citation: Keshavarz-Ghorabaee, M., Amiri, M., Zavadskas, E. K., Turskis, Z., Antucheviciene, J. (2021). Determination of objective weights using a new method based on the removal effects of criteria (MEREC). Symmetry, 13(4), 525.
source.location: Section 3 (Eqs. 1-6) and Section 4.1, Tables 2-4 and the text of Steps 3-6
source.note: Read from the publisher's PDF (CC BY).

notes: Criteria types are printed in Table 2: C1, C2 in B (beneficial), C3, C4 in H (non-beneficial).
Every criterion is transformed into a minimisation type: n = min/x for beneficial and x/max for non-beneficial criteria (Eq. 2), so smaller normalised values mean better performance.

Step 6 prints 'w1 = 1.71 / 2.97 = 0.5752'. The quotient of the rounded numbers is 0.5758; 0.5752 is E_1 / sum E with unrounded E (1.7087 / 2.9705). All four printed weights follow the unrounded values.
All x_ij must be > 0 (Step 1); the logarithm is undefined otherwise.
